USD.summary: Fed is balancing dual mandate with gradual recalibration. Rates held steady with cautious forward guidance on labor market resilience and persistent services inflation.

EUR.summary: ECB focused on stagnating growth in Germany and France while headline inflation converged to 2.0% target. Markets pricing further rate cuts.

JPY.summary: BoJ exited negative interest rates and YCC, pursuing slow normalization amid sustained wage growth ('shunto' results). Governor Ueda signaling additional hikes.

GBP.summary: BoE cut rates once to 4.75%, remaining vigilant on sticky wage pressures and fiscal budget announcements.

AUD.summary: RBA keeping cash rate elevated due to sticky trimmed-mean inflation and tight domestic labor conditions. Lagging other G10 central banks in cutting.

CAD.summary: BoC accelerated rate-cutting cycle with 50 bps cuts to counteract sluggish GDP per capita and household mortgage renewals.

CHF.summary: SNB lowered rates to curb excessive Swiss Franc strength and combat sub-1.5% inflation. Prepared to intervene in FX market if CHF appreciates further.

historical_cycles.explanation: The Federal Reserve initiates its first interest rate hike from 0.25%, while BoJ Governor Kuroda reaffirms negative interest rates and strict 10-year Yield Curve Control (YCC). The widening spread initiates the greatest currency carry trade of the decade.
historical_cycles.takeaway: Early in a monetary policy divergence, currency trends exhibit high persistence. Do not try to pick the top when yield spreads are accelerating.

historical_cycles.explanation: US inflation prints at 9.1%. The Fed raises rates in consecutive 75 bps increments. The US-Japan 2Y spread blows out beyond 400 basis points. USD/JPY gains over 2,500 pips in 6 months.
historical_cycles.takeaway: When 2-year yield spreads widen by >200 bps in a quarter, technical resistance levels routinely fail as institutional carry flows overwhelm order books.

historical_cycles.explanation: USD/JPY touches 151.94. Japan's Ministry of Finance conducts surprise direct market interventions, selling ~$43 Billion USD. Spot plunges 500 pips in minutes, but the fundamental yield spread remains at +445 bps.
historical_cycles.takeaway: Central bank interventions create short-term liquidity shocks, but unless the underlying yield spread narrows, the carry trade will re-accumulate at lower prices.

historical_cycles.explanation: Following the Silicon Valley Bank regional banking shock, US yields temporarily retreat. As banking stability returns, institutional funds re-enter USD/JPY carry trades at 138-140.
historical_cycles.takeaway: Market pullbacks toward the 20-day EMA on stable yield spreads represent institutional re-entry opportunities.

historical_cycles.explanation: US 'Higher-for-Longer' macro theme pushes US 10-year yields to 5.0% and 2-year yields to 5.2%. Carry trade returns reach record levels as Japanese retail investors ('Mrs. Watanabe') dump Yen.
historical_cycles.takeaway: When speculative positioning reaches historical net-short extremes on CME CoT reports, asymmetric downside tail risk begins to build.

historical_cycles.explanation: USD/JPY breaks 160.00 for the first time in 34 years. Japan's Ministry of Finance deploys over $62 Billion in interventions around the Golden Week holiday.
historical_cycles.takeaway: At round psycho-structural levels (155, 160) accompanied by MoF 'rate checks', options collars must be deployed to eliminate catastrophic downside tail risk.

historical_cycles.explanation: On July 31, BoJ surprises markets by hiking rates to 0.25%, while US July jobs report triggers the 'Sahm Rule' recession indicator. 2Y spread collapses 100 bps in days. Global carry trades violently liquidate; Nikkei drops 12% in a single day.
historical_cycles.takeaway: The death of a carry trade is violent and asymmetric. When the funding currency hikes while the target currency signals rate cuts, exit carry longs immediately.

historical_cycles.explanation: US economic exceptionalism re-emerges with strong non-farm payrolls. The 2Y spread stabilizes at +350 bps, allowing USD/JPY to recover back into the 150-153 zone.
historical_cycles.takeaway: Even after an unwind, if the residual yield spread remains wide (+350 bps), the carry incentive gradually reasserts itself once market volatility settles.
